title: Virtualized cost table: keyboard nav, ARIA, and i18n-ready number formatting
creator: Emma Chen
description:
Context: The Cost Explorer may render tens of thousands of rows for large orgs. We use windowed/virtualized rendering to keep the DOM small but current implementation breaks keyboard navigation, screen reader semantics, and locale-aware number formatting when rows or columns are recycled. This ticket designs a robust, accessible virtualized table component and interactions for the Console's cost tables.

Problem: Screen readers announce inconsistent row/column counts; keyboard users cannot reliably tab or arrow between rows when off-screen rows are remounted; columns with numeric values are not consistently formatted for different locales when the table lazily loads additional pages.

Goal: Deliver a design that: (1) preserves ARIA table semantics with virtualization, (2) defines keyboard patterns for row/column navigation + selection + range selection, (3) specifies accessible column-resize and column-reordering keyboard affordances, (4) ensures numbers, currency, and ranges are rendered with locale-specific formatting even as rows are dynamically materialized, and (5) includes performance-friendly announcement strategies for live-updates (no screen reader spam).
acceptance_criteria: Role and semantics: Virtualized table must expose role="table" at the container, aria-rowcount and aria-colcount must reflect the total dataset size, and each visible row must have role="row" and appropriate rowindex attributes.

Keyboard nav: Arrow keys move focus between cells; Home/End jump to row start/end; PageUp/PageDown move viewport and keep focus on the logically adjacent row; Shift+Arrow initiates range selection. Keyboard behavior documented and prototyped.
Focus preservation: When a focused row is virtualized out and then back in, focus must remain logically on the same row (no loss of context).

Screen reader announcements: New rows loaded via infinite scroll should not create noisy announcements; only significant updates (e.g., totals changed by >1%) create a concise live region announcement with locale-aware phrasing.

Number formatting: All numeric cells (cost, usage, percentage) must support ICU-style locale formatting via a data attribute + formatting utility; prototype demonstrates switching between en-US and fr-FR with identical virtualization behavior.
High contrast & reduced motion: Table interactions (focus rings, resize handles, drag previews) must have high-contrast tokens and reduced-motion alternatives documented.
Column ops: Column resizing and reordering must be operable with keyboard (resizer handle receives focus; Left/Right adjust size in 4px steps; Ctrl/Cmd+Arrow reorders).
Design deliverables: Figma prototype with keyboard/VO walkthrough, interaction spec, and acceptance checklist included in the ticket.
review_feedback: PM (Marco Alvarez): Good. Please ensure performance metrics (time-to-interactive) are tracked for 50k rows scenario.

Accessibility reviewer (Liam O'Connor): ARIA row/col counts approach looks correct but verify on NVDA+ChromeVox with voice settings; live region phrasing needs to avoid percentages when comma separators differ across locales.
Engineering (Sofia Martinez): Concern about focus syncing edge-case when server-sorted columns cause index shifts — propose using stable row IDs + focus mapping to ID rather than index.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Emma Chen: Initial design draft uploaded to Figma. Focus flow diagram added showing keyboard + VO narration for focused cell and row-level actions.

2026-03-04 — Priya Nair: Iterated the column-resize keyboard pattern per WCAG request: resizer handle is focusable and shows numeric size in an accessible tooltip; added accessible drag preview variant for reduced-motion users.

2026-03-06 — Liam O'Connor (a11y QA): Ran quick NVDA smoke test. Observed that aria-rowindex on recycled rows sometimes reports duplicate indices for 1-2 frames during fast scroll; recommended a debounce on aria updates until a stable render pass completes.
2026-03-08 — Sofia Martinez (Eng): Implemented dev spike confirming stable ID approach for focus retention. Pushed spike branch, linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4762
2026-03-09 — Emma Chen: Updated prototype to include locale toggle; added note to acceptance criteria to validate formatting against ICU patterns and currency fallback rules.
2026-03-10 — Priya Nair: Shared design for sign-off. Requested one more pass on live region language for non-English locales; flagged for translation review.
next_steps: 1) Engineering spike PR needs review (ENG-11894). 2) Accessibility QA: run test matrix across NVDA, VoiceOver, ChromeVox with en-US, fr-FR, ja-JP locales. 3) Implement aria-update debounce strategy and stable-id focus mapping. 4) Translation team to review live-region strings and pluralization templates.
